---
title: "Course content"
---

The course runs from air through water to soils and contaminants, with most
depth in water chemistry.

## Topic sequence and reading

Chapters refer to vanLoon and Duffy, *Environmental Chemistry: A Global
Perspective*, 4th edition (2017). Each unit's notes say which parts to read.

| Unit | Book chapters | Chemical focus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [1. Environmental amounts and balances](environmental-systems/notes.qmd) | 1 | Concentration, load, boundaries, and conservation. |
| [2. Reactions in the atmosphere](atmospheric-reactions/notes.qmd) | 2–4 | Photolysis, ozone cycles, catalysts, and rates. |
| [3. Atmospheric deposition and acidity](deposition/notes.qmd) | 5–7 | Oxidation, wet/dry transfer, and equivalent budgets. |
| [4. Molecules, radiation, and climate](climate-chemistry/notes.qmd) | 8 | Infrared absorption, spectra, particles, and persistence. |
| [5. Aquatic composition and equilibrium](aquatic-equilibria/notes.qmd) | 9–10 | Charge balance, activity, and simple speciation; activity A. |
| [6. Carbonate and gas chemistry](carbonate-gases/notes.qmd) | 10–11 | Carbonate, alkalinity, gas exchange, calcite; activity B. |
| [7. Organic matter in water](aquatic-organic-matter/notes.qmd) | 12 | Binding, colour, carbon, and oxygen demand. |
| [8. Metal speciation and mobility](metals/notes.qmd) | 13 | Ligands, hydrolysis, free ions, and solubility. |
| [9. Colloids, surfaces, and sorption](surfaces/notes.qmd) | 14 | Surface charge, partition balances, and mobility. |
| [10. Redox and environmental cycles](redox-cycles/notes.qmd) | 10, 13, 15 | Electron balances, nitrogen, iron, sulfur, and phosphate. |
| [11. Water pollution and treatment chemistry](water-treatment/notes.qmd) | 16 | Chemical transformations, separation, and residuals. |
| [12. Soil chemistry and retention](soil-chemistry/notes.qmd) | 17–18 | Exchange charge, mineral inventories, and acid response. |
| [13. Waste materials and leachate chemistry](waste-leachate/notes.qmd) | 19 | Sulfide oxidation, acidity, and neutralisation. |
| [14. Organic contaminants and environmental fate](organic-contaminants/notes.qmd) | 20 | Ionisation, partitioning, parent loss; activity C. |
| [15. Connecting air, catchments, and water](integrated-case/notes.qmd) | 21 and earlier | A chemical argument supported by budgets and evidence. |


## Three supporting computing activities

Three short activities in R, using the workflow from introductory computing.

| Activity | Files | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [A: water analysis](aquatic-equilibria/exercise.qmd#activity-a-water-table-in-r) | [Download ZIP](downloads/water-analysis.zip) | An ion table, charge checks, and a documented correction |
| [B: carbonate species](carbonate-gases/exercise.qmd#plot-the-chemical-prediction-in-r) | [Download ZIP](downloads/carbonate-speciation.zip) | A hand-checked distribution curve at prescribed pH |
| [C: contaminant fate](organic-contaminants/exercise.qmd#activity-c-a-fate-model-in-r) | [Download ZIP](downloads/contaminant-fate.zip) | A two-phase parent balance and reproducible chemical explanation |

Extract each ZIP into its own folder and open it as a project. Packages: `readr`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `rmarkdown`.
